task.title: Money Flow Wedge Scout
task.objective: Discover the strongest tiny programmable software/AI intervention inside an existing large private-sector money flow, continuously rank a best surviving hypothesis, attack it when all build gates appear satisfied, and persist every run so future runs continue from accumulated evidence rather than restarting.

operating_protocol.discovery_floor: Every run must return at least one best surviving hypothesis, even if some gates remain uncertain.
freeze_build_threshold: recurring measurable leakage or unrealized value
credible tiny fee stronger than obvious self-serve or flat-fee alternatives
no need to own the core transaction or request path
no dominant or sufficiently close incumbent or first-party feature
operating_protocol.search_behavior: Before threshold maintain a current leader and try to beat it. At threshold enter ATTACK and search for disconfirming evidence. If it survives, freeze and build; if it fails, record fatal flaw and promote the next candidate.
operating_protocol.persistence_rule: Every scheduled or manual run must append its normalized result, candidate scores, gate changes, evidence, rejected reasons, current leader and next research test to Taskman persistence before the run is considered complete.

conversation_history.summary: Opportunity search narrowed away from tenders, jobs, freelance lead hunting, buyer/seller matchmaking, manufacturer sourcing and generic demand creation toward programmable interventions in existing private money flows.
Adopted eight strict build gates and lifecycle SEARCH -> ATTACK -> FROZEN-BUILD.
Rejected after attack because trigger was customer-created, intervention sat on the request path, first-party cheaper lanes and gateways existed, and performance pricing was weak.
Added two-level standard: every run must return a best surviving hypothesis while final build threshold stays strict; search breadth widened and now drills flow -> state transition -> micro-decision.
Clean authorization/fulfillment/expiry trigger, later weakened by first-party capture/reauthorization features and payment orchestration.
Strong minimum-spend shortfall economics, later weakened by cloud commitment managers and procurement/SaaS allocation tooling.
Excellent economics but current systems reconcile volume commitments, deficiency payments and make-up rights.
Promising pattern: two legitimate future uses already exist and a contractual or quota state changes which is economically optimal; detect before the decision and redirect existing activity.
Prepaid messaging credits plus scheduled sends created a good trigger; later search found mature multi-provider SMS routing/cost optimization layers.
GitHub/Taskman selected as permanent anchor for search state, evidence, rejected paths, scores, task results and conversation-derived knowledge.
Every recurring research run must read Taskman first and persist the full normalized result back to Taskman before completion.

Included/prepaid SaaS or API capacity approaches reset while already-planned deferrable workloads exist; clean trigger and measurable overage avoidance, but no single high-value non-AI/non-enrichment vertical with proven leakage was identified.

App-store failed-renewal events and provider-native grace-period settings create a small configuration decision. For high-variable-cost subscription apps, longer grace can recover more renewals but also incur service cost for users who never recover. The open wedge is optimizing net margin from the grace duration, not generic dunning.

current_leader.name: Subscription grace-period cost/recovery optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: subscription renewal fails -> app-store retry/grace event appears -> developer has a provider-native grace-period duration setting while service continues -> longer grace increases recovery probability but may add variable service cost for subscribers who never recover -> recommend the duration that maximizes expected net subscription margin
current_leader.why_survived: The flow is large; billing failures are a major source of involuntary churn; Apple and Google expose configurable recovery windows and machine-readable billing states; the intervention can be read-only configuration intelligence; current dunning tools recover individual subscriptions but this search did not find a dominant product that optimizes the store-level grace duration using each app's recovery-by-day curve versus marginal cost-to-serve.
strongest_evidence: RevenueCat State of Subscription Apps 2026 reports billing failures are roughly a third of Google Play subscription cancellations and about 15% on the App Store in its dataset.
Google reports that extending decline recovery from 30 to 60 days produced an average 10% reduction in involuntary churn for renewals.
Apple allows 3, 16 or 28-day Billing Grace Period choices and exposes PATCH /v1/subscriptionGracePeriods/{id} to modify grace configuration.
RevenueCat exposes BILLING_ISSUE/grace and RENEWAL events, enabling machine-readable recovery curves without owning payment processing.
current_leader.closest_threat: For low-marginal-cost apps the optimal answer may simply be maximum grace, collapsing the wedge to a checkbox. Google already defaults grace on and promotes longer recovery windows. Subscription analytics/dunning platforms can also absorb the recommendation cheaply.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read billing-issue and renewal events plus app/cohort cost-to-serve; estimate recovery probability by day and expected net value for each available store grace setting; output the economically optimal configuration and expected net-margin change. Initially do not retry payments or message subscribers. With authorization, an Apple setting can later be changed through App Store Connect API.
current_leader.monetization: Small fee per configuration optimization cycle or capped share of measured incremental net margin. Percentage pricing is currently uncertain because app-wide settings make causal attribution noisier than event-level interventions.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Need proof that a meaningful population of high-variable-cost subscription apps has a non-trivial optimal grace duration. Apple settings are app-wide, so clean concurrent A/B attribution is difficult. If maximum grace dominates realistic economics, or an incumbent already optimizes this setting, kill the candidate.
current_leader.next_research_test: Model high-variable-cost mobile subscriptions using public recovery-by-day curves and realistic marginal service costs for AI/compute/licensed-content apps. Determine when 3 vs 16 vs 28 days changes expected net margin, then search exact grace-duration/configuration optimizers.

runner_ups.reason: Clean quota/reset trigger, but no single high-value non-AI/non-enrichment vertical with proven buyer-side leakage and easy scheduling has been found.
Real expiry but multi-provider routing software can absorb the expiry variable.
Excellent dollar signals, but current DER/battery/EV software already optimizes timing directly.

new_search_rules: Provider-native configurable recovery windows are interesting only when the optimal setting is economically non-obvious; otherwise the wedge collapses to a checkbox.
Optimize net-margin recovery, not gross renewal recovery, whenever continuing unpaid service creates real variable cost.
Treat app-wide configuration attribution as a first-class monetization gate because lack of per-user experiments can weaken performance pricing.
